summary: The main article describes a visible-light-mediated organocatalyzed 1,3-aminoacylation of cyclopropanes using N-benzoyl saccharin. It includes optimization tables, substrate scope figures for cyclopropanes and saccharin derivatives, and detailed mechanistic investigations including kinetic and quenching studies.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: Motivation for NHCs/PC dual-catalyzed addition of amide (C-N bonds) to cyclopropane. a Aminocarbonation of C-C multi-bonds employing unstrained bifunctional C-N reagents (via C-N bond cleavage). b Visible-light-driven photocatalysis in C-C activation of unactivated aryl cyclopropane. c General 1, 3-aminoacylation of cyclopropanes employing bifunctional N -acyl saccharin.
items.description: This figure outlines the background and motivation for the study, comparing previous work on C-N bond cleavage with the current approach for 1,3-aminoacylation of cyclopropanes.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Condition Optimizations a
items.description: This table summarizes the optimization of reaction conditions, including the screening of photocatalysts (PC), NHC catalysts, and solvents.

items.heading: Fig. 2
items.caption: Scope of the substrate a . a scope of cyclopropane. b scope of N -benzoylsaccharin.
items.description: This figure displays the substrate scope for various aryl cyclopropanes and N-benzoyl saccharin derivatives, showing the yields for products 3 through 59.

items.heading: Fig. 3
items.caption: Three-Component 1,3-Aminoacylation of Cyclopropane.
items.description: This figure illustrates the extension of the methodology to a three-component coupling reaction using benzoyl fluoride and various nitrogen sources.

items.heading: Fig. 4
items.caption: Synthetic applicability. a Large-scale synthesis. b Follow-up transformations.
items.description: This figure demonstrates the practical utility of the reaction through a gram-scale synthesis and several chemical transformations of the resulting γ-amino ketones.

items.heading: Fig. 5
items.caption: Mechanistic investigations. a Control experiment. b Preparation of NHC-adduct. c Catalistic acitivity of NHC-adduct. d Radical capture experiment. e Competing experiment. f Ring-opening of enantiomerically enriched 1-28, 1-32 . g Light on/off experiments. h Stern-Volmer quenching studies. i Excitation experiments with UV light. j The effect of PC (EPC+/PC) and cyclopropane (EOX) on reactivity. k Reaction progress kinetic analysis.
items.description: A comprehensive set of mechanistic studies including radical trapping, competition experiments, stereospecificity tests, and kinetic analysis to support the proposed catalytic cycle.

items.heading: Fig. 6
items.caption: Proposed catalytic cycle. Oxidative quenching driven NHC/PC dual catalysis.
items.description: This figure details the proposed dual catalytic cycle involving NHC-mediated C-N cleavage and photoredox-driven oxidative quenching to form C-C and C-N bonds.
